ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: By “clear signs” the people mean a palpable miracle, which they demand before accepting Hūd's claim or abandoning their deities.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: The words “clear signs” refer to a palpable miracle

STUDYQURAN:11:53/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:11:53/r1.speaker: Bḍ
STUDYQURAN:11:53/r1.claim: Bḍ explains a clear proof as evidence verifying Hūd’s claim to be a prophet sent by God.
STUDYQURAN:11:53/r1.anchor: clear evidence that testifies to the truthfulness of his claim to being a prophet sent by God (Bḍ)

STUDYQURAN:11:53/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:11:53/r2.speaker: Bḍ
STUDYQURAN:11:53/r2.claim: Bḍ says Hūd’s people failed to see his clear proofs because they obstinately rejected his message.
STUDYQURAN:11:53/r2.anchor: unable to see the clear proofs brought by Hūd because of their obstinacy in rejecting his message (Bḍ)

TAB-FULL:v12p446/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p446/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v12p446/r1.claim: Hud's people say he brought them no clear explanation or proof for his claims, so they will not concede that he truthfully calls them to worship God alone or that he is a prophet.
TAB-FULL:v12p446/r1.anchor: قال قوم هود لهود: يا هود ما أتيتنا ببيان، ولا برهان على ما تقول

TAB-FULL:v12p446/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p446/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v12p446/r2.claim: They will not abandon their deities because of what Hud says or on account of his words.
TAB-FULL:v12p446/r2.anchor: يقول: وما نحن بتاركي آلهتنا يعني لقولك: أو من أجل قولك

TAB-FULL:v12p446/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p446/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v12p446/r3.claim: They say they do not believe or affirm Hud's claim to prophethood and a message from God to them.
TAB-FULL:v12p446/r3.anchor: يقول: قالوا: وما نحن لك بما تدعي من النبوة والرسالة من الله إلينا بمصدقين

TABATABAI:11:53-55/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:53-55/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:53-55/r1.claim: The people of Hūd answer in general that he brought no proof or miraculous sign, so there is no reason to heed a call they consider unsupported.
TABATABAI:11:53-55/r1.anchor: يعنون أن دعوتك خالية عن الحجة والآية المعجزة ولا موجب للإصغاء إلى ما هذا شأنه

TABATABAI:11:53-55/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:53-55/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:53-55/r2.claim: Specifically, they refuse to abandon their partners, and refuse to believe in or obey Hūd, rejecting both parts of his appeal.

TABATABAI:11:53-56/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:53-56/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:53-56/r1.claim: Hūd’s answer addresses their demand that he brought no proof: his challenge and disavowal answer the objection rather than leave it unanswered.
TABATABAI:11:53-56/r1.anchor: ومن المستبعد جدا أن يهمل النبي هود عليه السلام في دعوته وحجته التعرض للجواب عنه

TABATABAI:11:50-60#2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:50-60#2/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:50-60#2/r1.claim: ʿĀd were prehistoric Arab inhabitants of the peninsula; their history survives only in unreliable tales, and the extant Torah does not mention them.
TABATABAI:11:50-60#2/r1.anchor: عاد قوم هود هؤلاء قوم من العرب من بشر ما قبل التاريخ كانوا يسكنون الجزيرة انقطعت أخبارهم وانمحت آثارهم

TABATABAI:11:50-60#2/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:50-60#2/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:50-60#2/r2.claim: The Quran places ʿĀd after Noah in al-Aḥqāf; the name may be “first ʿĀd,” suggesting a second ʿĀd as well.
TABATABAI:11:50-60#2/r2.anchor: كانوا قوما يسكنون الأحقاف من شبه جزيرة العرب بعد قوم نوح

TABATABAI:11:50-60#2/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:50-60#2/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:50-60#2/r3.claim: The people were tall, strong, and physically imposing, with advanced urban life, thriving towns, fertile land, gardens, date palms, and crops.
TABATABAI:11:50-60#2/r3.anchor: كانت لهم أجساد طويلة وكانوا ذوي بسطة في الخلق أولي قوة وبطش شديد وكان لهم تقدم ورقي في المدينة والحضارة

TABATABAI:11:50-60#2/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:50-60#2/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:50-60#2/r4.claim: After enjoying God’s bounty, they developed idolatry, built monuments on every rise and grand structures as if to live forever, and obeyed arrogant tyrants.
TABATABAI:11:50-60#2/r4.anchor: لم يزل القوم يتنعمون بنعمة الله حتى غيروا ما بأنفسهم فتعرقت فيهم الوثنية وبنوا بكل ريع آية يعبثون

TABATABAI:11:50-60#2/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:50-60#2/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:50-60#2/r5.claim: God sent their kinsman Hūd to call them to truth, worship of God, rejection of idols, justice, and mercy; he admonished them and made the way clear.
TABATABAI:11:50-60#2/r5.anchor: فبعث الله إليهم أخاهم هودا يدعوهم إلى الحق ويرشدهم إلى أن يعبدوا الله ويرفضوا الأوثان

TABATABAI:11:50-60#2/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:50-60#2/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:50-60#2/r6.claim: Only a small group believed; most persisted in defiance, called Hūd foolish and mad, and demanded the threatened punishment, to which he replied that its timing belongs to God.
TABATABAI:11:50-60#2/r6.anchor: وأصر جمهورهم على البغي والعناد، ورموه بالسفه والجنون

TABATABAI:11:50-60#2/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:50-60#2/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:50-60#2/r7.claim: God sent a barren, furious wind through adverse days, lasting seven nights and eight days; it left the people fallen like hollow palm trunks and destroyed them all but their dwellings.
TABATABAI:11:50-60#2/r7.anchor: وأرسل إليهم الريح العقيم ما تذر من شيء أتت عليه إلا جعلته كالرميم

TABATABAI:11:50-60#2/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:50-60#2/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:50-60#2/r8.claim: They first mistook the cloud approaching their valleys for rain, but it was the very calamity they had demanded; God annihilated them and saved Hūd and the believers by His mercy.
TABATABAI:11:50-60#2/r8.anchor: وكانوا بادئ ما رأوه عارضا مستقبل أوديتهم استبشروا وقالوا عارض ممطرنا وقد أخطأوا بل كان هو الذي استعجلوا به

TABATABAI:11:50-60#2/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:50-60#2/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:50-60#2/r9.claim: Hūd was from ʿĀd and the second prophet whose struggle against idolatry and suffering for God the Quran narrates; God praises him among the noble messengers.
TABATABAI:11:50-60#2/r9.anchor: وأما هود عليه السلام فهو من قوم عاد وثاني الأنبياء الذين انتهضوا للدفاع عن الحق ودحض الوثنية ممن ذكر الله قصته وما قاساه

TABRISI:11:50-60#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:50-60#2/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:11:50-60#2/r7.claim: The people say Hud brought no clear proof or miracle that would establish his truthfulness.

TABRISI:11:50-60#2/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:50-60#2/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:11:50-60#2/r8.claim: One grammatical explanation makes “ʿan” stand in place of “bāʾ,” so the meaning is “because of your statement.”
TABRISI:11:50-60#2/r8.anchor: إن عن جعلت مكان الباء فمعناه بقولك

TABRISI:11:50-60#2/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:50-60#2/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:11:50-60#2/r9.claim: They reject the proof because they imitate ancestors and leaders, dismiss its bearer without examining the evidence, doubt its validity, and hold false premises leading them to deny it.

TABRISI:11:50-60#2/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:50-60#2/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:11:50-60#2/r10.claim: They worship idols because they think these bring them near God, Satan promises worldly favor through them, or anthropomorphist ideas lead them to make idols in the imagined divine form.
TABRISI:11:50-60#2/r10.anchor: أشياء منها اعتقادهم أن عبادتها تقربهم إلى الله زلفى

TABRISI:11:50-60#2/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:50-60#2/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:11:50-60#2/r11.claim: Their declaration means that they do not believe or affirm Hud's message.
TABRISI:11:50-60#2/r11.anchor: أي مصدقين وإنما حملهم على دفع البينة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p445#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p445#2/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p445#2/r1.claim: They deny that Hud brought a clear proof distinguishing truth from falsehood; this is slander, transgression, and refusal to accept evidence.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p445#2/r1.anchor: أي بحجة واضحة نفصل بها الحق من الباطل. وهذا بهت منهم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p445#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p445#2/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p445#2/r2.claim: Here عن means by, as the prepositions عن and باء can alternate; the same usage occurs in 7:187 and 25:59.

QASHANI:11:52-53/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:11:52-53/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:11:52-53/r5.claim: They deny Hud's clear proof because natural veils limit their understanding and blind their inner sight, preventing them from grasping its demonstration.
QASHANI:11:52-53/r5.anchor: لقصور فهمهم وعمى بصيرتهم عن إدراك البرهان لمكان الغشاوات الطبيعية وإذا لم يدركوه أنكروه

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:11:52-55/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:11:52-55/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:11:52-55/r4.claim: They denied Hud's prophethood and claimed he had brought no clear proof.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:11:52-55/r4.anchor: منكرين لنبوته: { يا هود ما جئتنا ببينة } بحجة واضحة

ELMALILI:11:53-57/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:11:53-57/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:11:53-57/r1.claim: Hud's people say he brought no clear proof, refuse to abandon their idols at his word, and refuse to believe him.
ELMALILI:11:53-57/r1.anchor: Ve biz senin sözünden dolayı ilâhlarımızı terk etmeyiz. {وَمَا نَحْنُ لَكَ بِمُؤْمِنِينَ} Biz sana inanmayız.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:53/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:53/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:53/r1.claim: Hud presented rational proofs and miracles to establish his prophethood; although the Qur'an does not specify those miracles, it says his people denied them.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:53/r1.anchor: Kur’an-ı Kerîm bu mûcizelerin ne olduğunu bildirmemiş olmakla birlikte Hûd’un getirdiği mûcizeleri kavminin inkâr ettiğini haber vermektedir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:53/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:53/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:53/r2.claim: His people dismissed his miracles and rational arguments and refused his call, saying they would neither abandon their gods because of him nor believe him.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:53/r2.anchor: Kavmi onun getirdiği mûcizelere ve kullandığı aklî delillere değer vermedi ve çağrısını reddetti

BURHAN:v4p286/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p286/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p286/r6.claim: ʿAn can mark cause: Abraham's prayer followed a promise, and Lot's people say they will not abandon their gods because of Muhammad's statement.
BURHAN:v4p286/r6.anchor: وما نحن بتاركي آلهتنا عن قولك

BURHAN:v3p336/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p336/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p336/r1.claim: Hud shifts from the statement “I call God to witness” to the command “you witness”: God's testimony affirms monotheism, while addressing the idolaters this way shows disregard for their religion.
BURHAN:v3p336/r1.anchor: ولا شك أن معنى إشهاد الله على البراءة صحيح في معنى يثبت التوحيد بخلاف إشهادهم

ITQAN:v2p479/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p479/r3.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p479/r3.claim: عن can express cause: the people will not leave their gods because of Hud's words, and Abraham's prayer was because of a promise.
ITQAN:v2p479/r3.anchor: أي لأجل موعدة ﴿ وما نحن بتاركي آلهتنا عن قولك ﴾ أي لقولك

ITQAN:v3p152#3/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p152#3/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p152#3/r1.claim: Concision can arise from restriction, conjunction, passive voice, pronouns, a verb governing a complement clause, ellipsis in coordination or objects, interrogative and conditional particles, generic words, and dual or plural forms.
ITQAN:v3p152#3/r1.anchor: أن من أنواع إيجاز القصر باب الحصر سواء كان بإلا أو بإنما

ITQAN:v3p152#3/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p152#3/r2.speaker: ابن أبي الإصبع
ITQAN:v3p152#3/r2.claim: Ibn Abi al-Isba also counts interpretive breadth as a form of concision: wording supports several possible meanings, as with the openings of sūras.
ITQAN:v3p152#3/r2.anchor: مما يصلح أن يعد من أنواعه المسمى بالاتساع من أنواع البديع وهو أن يؤتى بكلام يتسع فيه التأويل

ITQAN:v1p252/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p252/r5.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p252/r5.claim: Nūn assimilates into rā or lām after a vowel and is otherwise clear, except nūn in naḥnu, which assimilates because it recurs often, repeats nūn, stays vocalized, and is heavy.
ITQAN:v1p252/r5.anchor: لكثرة دورها وتكرار النون فيها ولزوم حركتها وثقلها

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p438/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p438/r1.speaker: أبو زكريا
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p438/r1.claim: Abū Zakariyyā says ʿan fundamentally indicates passing beyond: speech reaches a listener from someone, and turning from Zayd means passing him.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p438/r1.anchor: قال أبو زكريا : معنى ' عن ' المجاوزة

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p438/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p438/r2.speaker: أبو زكريا
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p438/r2.claim: Abū Zakariyyā says ʿan is a preposition unless preceded by min; after min it is a noun because one preposition does not govern another.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p438/r2.anchor: وهي حرف ما لم يدخل عليها ' من ' فإذا دخلت

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p438/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p438/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p438/r5.claim: ʿAn can carry the sense of bi, 'because of' or 'by'.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p438/r5.anchor: والثاني : بمعنى ' الباء ' ومنه قوله تعالى في هود

SAMIN-DURR:11:53/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:53/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:11:53/r1.claim: ببينة may attach to جئتنا, meaning they were shown no proof, or modify an omitted state such as مستقرا or ملتبسا ببينة.
SAMIN-DURR:11:53/r1.anchor: يجوز أن تكون الباء للتعدية، فيتعلق بالفعل قبلها، أي: ما أظهرت لنا بينة قط.

SAMIN-DURR:11:53/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:53/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:11:53/r2.claim: عن قولك is preferably circumstantial from the pronoun in تاركي, meaning they leave their idols while turning from his statement; alternatively عن is causal and attaches to تاركي.
SAMIN-DURR:11:53/r2.anchor: حال من الضمير في " تاركي " ، أي: وما نترك آلهتنا صادرين عن قولك.

SAMIN-DURR:11:53/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:53/r3.speaker: ابن عطية
SAMIN-DURR:11:53/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya suggests a causal عن, while al-Zamakhsharī mentions only the preferred circumstantial analysis.
SAMIN-DURR:11:53/r3.anchor: وقد أشار إلى التعليل ابن عطية، ولكن المختار الأول، ولم يذكر الزمخشري غيره.

SIBAWAYH:تقولرويدزيداوإنماتريدأرودزيدا|ق.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:تقولرويدزيداوإنماتريدأرودزيدا|ق.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:تقولرويدزيداوإنماتريدأرودزيدا|ق.claim: Bare رويد occupies the position of a verb and means أرود in commands such as رويد زيدا.
SIBAWAYH:تقولرويدزيداوإنماتريدأرودزيدا|ق.anchor: تقول رويد زيدا وإنما تريد أرود زيدا

SIBAWAYH:تقولرويدزيداوإنماتريدأرودزيدا|ق.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:تقولرويدزيداوإنماتريدأرودزيدا|ق.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:تقولرويدزيداوإنماتريدأرودزيدا|ق.claim: رويد can modify an explicit verbal noun as an adverb, or stand alone with the verbal noun omitted; with an expressed noun it can function in more than one way.
SIBAWAYH:تقولرويدزيداوإنماتريدأرودزيدا|ق.anchor: ويكون رويد أيضا صفة كقولك ساروا سيرا رويدا

SIBAWAYH:تقولرويدزيداوإنماتريدأرودزيدا|ق.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:تقولرويدزيداوإنماتريدأرودزيدا|ق.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:تقولرويدزيداوإنماتريدأرودزيدا|ق.claim: The attached kaf in رويدك specifies or emphasizes the addressee, distinguishing a particular listener when the form itself does not mark person or number.
SIBAWAYH:تقولرويدزيداوإنماتريدأرودزيدا|ق.anchor: أدخل الكاف حين خاف التباس من يعنى بمن لا يعنى وإنما حذفها

SIBAWAYH:تقولرويدزيداوإنماتريدأرودزيدا|ق.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:تقولرويدزيداوإنماتريدأرودزيدا|ق.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:تقولرويدزيداوإنماتريدأرودزيدا|ق.claim: The kaf is neither a subject marker nor a noun: the implicit command subject is a doer, and treating kaf as a noun creates impossible constructions.
SIBAWAYH:تقولرويدزيداوإنماتريدأرودزيدا|ق.anchor: المضمرين ها هنا فاعلون وعلامة المضمرين

SIBAWAYH:تقولرويدزيداوإنماتريدأرودزيدا|ق.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:تقولرويدزيداوإنماتريدأرودزيدا|ق.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:تقولرويدزيداوإنماتريدأرودزيدا|ق.claim: In هلم لك, unlike رويدك, kaf is a genitive noun after لام; its meaning still adds specification or emphasis.
SIBAWAYH:تقولرويدزيداوإنماتريدأرودزيدا|ق.anchor: هلم لك فالكاف ههنا اسم مجرور باللام

SIBAWAYH:تقولرويدزيداوإنماتريدأرودزيدا|ق.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:تقولرويدزيداوإنماتريدأرودزيدا|ق.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:تقولرويدزيداوإنماتريدأرودزيدا|ق.claim: With a hidden nominative addressee, coordination and emphasis are smoother when that pronoun is made explicit, as in رويدكم أنتم وعبد الله.
SIBAWAYH:تقولرويدزيداوإنماتريدأرودزيدا|ق.anchor: وتقول فيما يكون معطوفا على الاسم المضمر فى النية

SIBAWAYH:تقولرويدزيداوإنماتريدأرودزيدا|ق.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:تقولرويدزيداوإنماتريدأرودزيدا|ق.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:تقولرويدزيداوإنماتريدأرودزيدا|ق.claim: A visible noun cannot coordinate directly with the genitive kaf in هلم لك; it can instead coordinate with the understood nominative addressee, made explicit by أنت.
SIBAWAYH:تقولرويدزيداوإنماتريدأرودزيدا|ق.anchor: ولا يجوز أن تعطف على الكاف المجرورة الاسم لأنك لا تعطف المظهر على المضمر

NASHR:v1p294/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p294/r2.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p294/r2.claim: When the letter before mīm has a vowel, mīm before bā is made quiescent and concealed with nasalization to avoid successive vowels; when the preceding letter is quiescent, the general rule is to leave it clear.
NASHR:v1p294/r2.anchor: تسكن عند الباء إذا تحرك ما قبلها

NASHR:v1p294/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p294/r3.speaker: القصباني عن شجاع عن أبي عمرو
NASHR:v1p294/r3.claim: Al-Qasbani from Shuja from Abu Amr reports concealment after a madd or lin letter, but this route is outside the book’s transmissions.
NASHR:v1p294/r3.anchor: إلا ما رواه القصباني، عن شجاع، عن أبي عمرو من الإخفاء

NASHR:v1p294/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p294/r4.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p294/r4.claim: Some earlier scholars called this concealment idgham; the author says ikhfa is the correct term and defers fuller discussion.
NASHR:v1p294/r4.anchor: وقد عبر بعض المتقدمين عن هذا الإخفاء بالإدغام

NASHR:v1p294/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p294/r5.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p294/r5.claim: Nūn assimilates into rāʾ or lām when the preceding letter is vowelled, but remains clear when the preceding letter is quiescent.
NASHR:v1p294/r5.anchor: تدغم إذا تحرك ما قبلها في الراء واللام

NASHR:v1p294/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p294/r6.speaker: أصحاب اليزيدي عن أبي عمرو
NASHR:v1p294/r6.claim: They assimilate the final nūn of نحن into lām only in ten occurrences; other than this word, a quiescent preceding letter prevents assimilation.
NASHR:v1p294/r6.anchor: إلا في كلمة نحن حيث وقعت وجملته عشرة مواضع

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p167/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p167/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p167/r1.claim: بينة means a clear proof or argument demonstrating the truth of Hud's claim.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p167/r1.anchor: ببينة أو بحجة واضحة تدل على صدقك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p167/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p167/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p167/r2.claim: Hud's opponents lie when they claim he brought no proof, just as Quraysh did, since Hud and other prophets had miracles even if not all are specified here.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p167/r2.anchor: وقد كذبوا في ذلك وبهتوه كما كذبت قريش في قولهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p167/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p167/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p167/r3.claim: Another explanation is that their blindness to truth and failure to consider the signs made them deny that any sign was a sign.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p167/r3.anchor: أو لعمائهم عن الحق وعدم نظرهم في الآيات اعتقدوا ما هو آية ليس بآية

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p167/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p167/r4.speaker: النبي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p167/r4.claim: The Prophet says every prophet received signs of a kind through which people believed; no grading is stated here.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p167/r4.anchor: قول رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «ما من نبي إلا وقد أوتي من الآيات ما مثله آمن عليه البشر»

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p167/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p167/r5.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p167/r5.claim: Zamakhshari parses عن قولك as a circumstantial phrase attached to the pronoun in تاركي: they would leave their gods departing from your saying.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p167/r5.anchor: عن في عن قولك حال من الضمير في تاركي آلهتنا، كأنه قيل: صادرين عن قولك، قاله الزمخشري.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p167/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p167/r6.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p167/r6.claim: Ibn Atiyya takes عن as causal, attached to تاركي: Hud's unsupported word would not cause them to abandon their gods.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p167/r6.anchor: وقد أشار إلى التعليل والسبب فيها ابن عطية، فقال: أي لا يكون قولك سببا لتركنا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p167/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p167/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p167/r7.claim: The next clause reinforces the opponents' effort to extinguish Hud's hope that they will enter his religion.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p167/r7.anchor: والجملة بعدها تأكيد وتقنيط له من دخولهم في دينه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p167/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p167/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p167/r8.claim: They explain Hud's call to worship Allah alone as madness inflicted by their gods because he insulted them and urged people to abandon their worship.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p167/r8.anchor: ثم نسبوا ما صدر منه من دعائهم إلى الله وإفراده بالألوهية إلى الخبل والجنون، وأن ذلك مما اعتراه به بعض آلهتهم

ALUSI-FULL:v12p81#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p81#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p81#2/r1.claim: The people of Hud deny he brought clear proof either from stubborn resistance or because they are so blind to truth and inattentive to the signs that they misjudge a miracle; the prophets in fact brought manifest signs and miracles.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p81#2/r1.anchor: وإنما قالوه لفرط عنادهم أو لشدة عماهم عن الحق وعدم نظرهم في الآيات

ALUSI-FULL:v12p81#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p81#2/r2.speaker: النبي
ALUSI-FULL:v12p81#2/r2.claim: A prophetic report says every prophet was given signs of the kind by which people believed; al-Alusi invokes it to explain that the signs were real even when this passage does not name them.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p81#2/r2.anchor: ففي الخبر ما من نبي إلا وقد أوتي من الآيات ما مثله آمن عليه البشر

ALUSI-FULL:v12p81#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p81#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p81#2/r3.claim: Leaving their gods means abandoning worship of them, and they say they will not do so because of Hud's bare assertion, unsupported by proof; here 'an' marks causation and attaches to 'leaving.'
ALUSI-FULL:v12p81#2/r3.anchor: فعن للتعليل كما قيل في قوله تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v12p81#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p81#2/r4.speaker: بعض المحققين
ALUSI-FULL:v12p81#2/r4.claim: Some careful grammarians attach the prepositional phrase to an omitted circumstantial 'departing from,' rather than directly to 'leaving.'
ALUSI-FULL:v12p81#2/r4.anchor: وذهب بعض المحققين إلى أنه متعلق بمحذوف وقع حالا من الضمير المستتر فيه أي صادرين

ALUSI-FULL:v12p81#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p81#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p81#2/r5.claim: The terms for departing from and returning to water became metaphors for acting and conducting affairs; a cited line uses issuing and drawing water as a metaphor for sound judgment in managing matters.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p81#2/r5.anchor: وقد شاع في كلامهم استعمال الصدر والورد كناية عن العمل والتصرف

ALUSI-FULL:v12p81#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p81#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p81#2/r6.claim: Arabic can omit the word for returning to water because departure entails it, as in the saying that someone acts only on another's judgment; the phrase then means they will not leave their gods while acting on Hud's word.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p81#2/r6.anchor: وقد يكتفى بالصد في ذلك لإستلزامه للورد فيقولون : لا يصدر إلا عن رأيه

ALUSI-FULL:v12p81#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p81#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p81#2/r7.claim: On that analysis, negation applies both to the restriction and the main clause: they will neither leave their gods nor act on Hud's saying.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p81#2/r7.anchor: والنفي فيه راجع إلى القيد والمقيد جميعا لأنهم لا يتركون آلهتهم ولا يعملون بقوله

ALUSI-FULL:v12p81#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p81#2/r8.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v12p81#2/r8.claim: Another view takes 'departing' to mean turning away, as a restriction on the negation, so they deny leaving their gods while turning away from Hud's words; it also answers Hud's command not to turn away.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p81#2/r8.anchor: وقيل : إن صادرين بمعنى معرضين وهو قيد للنفي والمعنى انتفى تركنا عبادة آلهتنا معرضين ( عن قولك )

ALUSI-FULL:v12p81#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p81#2/r9.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v12p81#2/r9.claim: Some analyze the construction as semantic inclusion rather than an omitted complement; al-Zamakhshari's wording appears to support this, as al-Kashf explains.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p81#2/r9.anchor: وجعل بعضهم إرادة ذلك من باب التضمين لا من باب تقدير المتعلق بقرينة ( عن )

ALUSI-FULL:v12p81#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p81#2/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p81#2/r10.claim: They mean either that they do not believe what Hud brought or that they believe nothing he says or does, which includes his message.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p81#2/r10.anchor: أي بمصدقين فيما جئت به أو في كل ما تأتي وتذر ويندرج فيه ذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v12p81#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p81#2/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p81#2/r11.claim: They repeat their refusal to believe with a nominal sentence, added bā, and a fronted subject for emphasis, signaling that no hope of their believing remains.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p81#2/r11.anchor: ثم كرروا ما دل عليه الكلام السابق من عدم إيمانهم بالجملة الاسمية مع زيادة الباء

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p183/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p183/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p183/r1.claim: They tell Hūd that he has brought no clear proof or argument for his claim.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p183/r1.anchor: ما جئتنا ببينة} أي: ببرهان وحجة واضحة على ما تقول

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p183/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p183/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p183/r2.claim: They will not abandon their gods merely because Hūd says so.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p183/r2.anchor: وما نحن بتاركي آلهتنا عن قولك} أي: بقولك

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p183/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p183/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p183/r3.claim: They say they will not believe Hūd.

BAYDAWI-FULL:11:53-55/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:53-55/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:53-55/r1.claim: They deny proof out of extreme obstinacy and disregard even the miracles brought to them.
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:53-55/r1.anchor: بحجة تدل على صحة دعواك وهو لفرط عنادهم

BAYDAWI-FULL:11:53-55/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:53-55/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:53-55/r2.claim: They refuse to abandon their idols’ worship at Hud’s word; the phrase describes their state as they refuse.
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:53-55/r2.anchor: صادرين عن قولك حال من الضمير في تاركي

BAYDAWI-FULL:11:53-55/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:53-55/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:53-55/r3.claim: Their words are meant to make Hud despair of their response or belief.

BIQAI-FULL:v3p542/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p542/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p542/r1.claim: After Hūd gave advice with utmost clarity and showed signs that would ordinarily convince people, the only answer was rejection.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p542/r1.anchor: جوابهم إلا أن { قالوا } اي عاد بعد أن أظهر لهم هود عليه السلام منا لمعجزات

BIQAI-FULL:v3p542/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p542/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p542/r2.claim: Calling him by his bare name instead of an honorific expresses harshness and rudeness.

BIQAI-FULL:v3p542/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p542/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p542/r3.claim: Their denial shows obstinate resistance to clear reason and transmitted proof, like the Arabs' demand for a sign despite the Prophet's innumerable signs (13:7).
BIQAI-FULL:v3p542/r3.anchor: { ما جئتنا ببينة } فأوضحوا لكل ذي لب أنهم مكابرون لقويم العقل وصريح النقل

BIQAI-FULL:v3p542/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p542/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p542/r4.claim: They say they will neither move beyond nor turn away from their idols because of Hūd's statement.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p542/r4.anchor: { وما نحن } وأغرقوا في النفي فقالوا : { بتاركي آلهتنا } مجاوزين لها أو صادرين { عن قولك }

BIQAI-FULL:v3p542/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p542/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p542/r5.claim: Biqāʿī notes their use of waw instead of causal fa, which would make the first statement the cause of the second.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p542/r5.anchor: وتركهم للعطف بالفاء - المؤذنة بأن الأول سبب الثاني اي الواو في قولهم : { وما نحن لك }

BIQAI-FULL:v3p542/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p542/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p542/r6.claim: The emphatic negation and nominal sentence portray settled defiance; they refuse to follow Hūd out of obstinacy rather than sincere belief that he lacked a proof.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p542/r6.anchor: دليل على أنهم تركوا إتباعه عنادا , لا أنهم يعتقدون أنه لم يأت ببينة

BIQAI-FULL:v3p542/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p542/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p542/r7.claim: Bayyina is a clear proof that distinguishes truth from falsehood; bayān separates a meaning from others until it is clarified to the mind.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p542/r7.anchor: والبينة : الحجة الواضحة في الفصل بينا لحق والباطل , والبيان : فصل المعنى من غيره

BIQAI-FULL:v3p542/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p542/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p542/r8.claim: People reject manifest proofs by suppressing doubt, imitating leaders, accusing the source, adopting corrupt premises, or acting from envy; all these causes share the presence of doubt.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p542/r8.anchor: مما سواه , والحامل على ترك البينة بعد ظهورها صد الشبهة عنها

IBNABIHATIM:v6p2046/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2046/r1.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2046/r1.claim: Said ibn Jubayr glosses believers here as those who accept the truth.
IBNABIHATIM:v6p2046/r1.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير قوله : بمؤمنين قال : بمصدقين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p97#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p97#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p97#2/r1.claim: The people's reply answers Hud's call; the sentence begins without a conjunction because it is dialogue responding to his invitation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p97#2/r1.anchor: بجواب عن دعوته ، ولذلك جردت الجملة عن العاطف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p97#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p97#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p97#2/r2.claim: Their opening address marks the importance of what follows and treats Hud as distant through heedlessness; it may also reproach and blame him, either figuratively or through literal and figurative address together.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p97#2/r2.anchor: يشير إلى الاهتمام بما سيقولونه ، وأنه جدير بأن يتنبه له

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p97#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p97#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p97#2/r3.claim: Their denial of proof is slander: Hud brought signs, as 11:59 indicates, although the Quran does not identify a particular sign; it may have been his prediction of exceptional abundance and uninterrupted fertility.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p97#2/r3.anchor: بهتان لأنه أتاهم بمعجزات لقوله تعالى : { وتلك عاد جحدوا بآيات ربهم }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p97#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p97#2/r4.speaker: محمد
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p97#2/r4.claim: An authentic hadith says every prophet was given signs like those through which people believed; Ibn Ashur cites it while discussing Hud's signs.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p97#2/r4.anchor: إلا أوتي من الآيات ما مثله آمن عليه البشر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p97#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p97#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p97#2/r5.claim: They meant Hud's signs did not match their demands; they present that as a reason for keeping their gods, but not as a logical inference from having seen no sign.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p97#2/r5.anchor: وإنما أرادوا أن البينات التي جاءهم بها هود عليه السلام لم تكن طبقا لمقترحاتهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p97#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p97#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p97#2/r6.claim: عن indicates departure: they will not leave their gods by reason of Hud's words, making his speech the proposed cause for abandoning them.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p97#2/r6.anchor: لا نتركها تركا صادرا عن قولك

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p180#3/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p180#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p180#3/r1.claim: The people of Hūd mean that he brought no sign compelling them to believe; in their blindness they deny that his miracles qualify as signs.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p180#3/r1.anchor: ما جئتنا بآية تضطرنا إلى الإيمان بك ونفوا أن تكون معجزاته آية بحسب ظنهم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p180#3/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p180#3/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p180#3/r2.claim: Their denial resembles Quraysh calling the Quran magic or poetry.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p180#3/r2.anchor: كما جعلت قريش القرآن سحرا وشعرا ونحو هذا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p180#3/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p180#3/r3.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p180#3/r3.claim: A Prophetic hadith says each prophet received signs like those by which people believed; this entails that Hūd and the other messengers had miracles, even if none are specified here.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p180#3/r3.anchor: وقد قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «ما من نبي إلا وقد أوتي من الآيات ما مثله آمن عليه البشر»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p180#3/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p180#3/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p180#3/r4.claim: They will not abandon their idols because of Hūd’s statement, which they regard as unsupported by a sign.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p180#3/r4.anchor: أي لا يكون قولك سبب تركنا إذ هو مجرد عن آية

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p117#3/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p117#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p117#3/r1.claim: Hūd's people say he brought no clear proof or argument.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p117#3/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى ﴿ ما جئتنا ببينة ﴾ أي بحجة واضحة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p117#3/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p117#3/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p117#3/r2.claim: Their gods are the idols they worship.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p117#3/r2.anchor: ﴿ وما نحن بتاركي آلهتنا ﴾ يعنون الأصنام

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p117#3/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p117#3/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p117#3/r3.claim: The phrase means they will not leave their idols because of what Hūd says; the prepositions ʿan and bāʾ can substitute for one another.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p117#3/r3.anchor: ﴿ عن قولك ﴾ أي بقولك والباء وعن يتعاقبان

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p329#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p329#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p329#2/r1.claim: Hud's people say he brought no proof, they will not abandon their gods merely because he tells them to, and they will not believe him.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p329#2/r1.anchor: أنهم قالوا لنبيهم: {ما جئتنا ببينة} أي: بحجة

JISHUMI:v5p3513/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3513/r12.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3513/r12.claim: The people of Ad claim that Hud brought no proof or miracle they could acknowledge; the claim is false because reflection reveals the proof, while doubts, imitation of leaders, and false premises divert them from considering it.
JISHUMI:v5p3513/r12.anchor: قالوا يعني: كفار عاد ياهود ما جئتنا ببينة بحجة ومعجزة فنقر لك؛ وذلك لأنهم لم يعدوا ما جاء به برهانا لقلة التدبر، وهذا كذب منهم

JISHUMI:v5p3513/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3513/r13.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3513/r13.claim: They say they will not stop worshipping idols simply because Hud says their worship is false and commands them to leave it.
JISHUMI:v5p3513/r13.anchor: وما نحن بتاركي آلهتنا عن قولك يعني: لا نترك عبادة الأوثان لقولك إنه باطل، وأمرك بتركه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p381#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p381#2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p381#2/r1.claim: Their claim that Hūd brought no clear proof is a lie and denial, like Quraysh demanding a sign despite the Prophet’s many signs.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p381#2/r1.anchor: كذب منهم وجحود ، كما قالت قريش لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p381#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p381#2/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p381#2/r2.claim: عن قولك is circumstantial: they will not abandon their gods in response to Hūd’s words, and they do not consider people like themselves fit to believe him.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p381#2/r2.anchor: حال من الضمير في تاركي آلهتنا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p381#2/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p381#2/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p381#2/r3.claim: Their words aim to extinguish Hūd’s hope that they will accept his call.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p381#2/r3.anchor: وما يصح من أمثالنا أن يصدقوا مثلك فيما يدعوهم إليه

MUQATIL:11:53-55/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:11:53-55/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:11:53-55/r1.claim: The people of Hud say he brought no clear proof that God had sent him to them.
MUQATIL:11:53-55/r1.anchor: يعني ببيان أنك رسول إلينا من الله

MUQATIL:11:53-55/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:11:53-55/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:11:53-55/r2.claim: They mean they will not stop worshipping idols merely because Hud says so, and they will not believe that he is a messenger.
MUQATIL:11:53-55/r2.anchor: ما نحن بتاركي آلهتنا عن قولك

NASAFI-FULL:v2p160/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p160/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p160/r1.claim: Their claim that Hūd brought no proof is a lie despite the many signs; Quraysh made a similar demand of the Prophet.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p160/r1.anchor: كذب منهم وجحود كما قالت قريش لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لولا أنزل عليه آية من ربه مع فوت آياته الحصر

NASAFI-FULL:v2p160/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p160/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p160/r2.claim: The clause is circumstantial to the pronoun in “abandoning”: they will not leave their gods on the basis of his word.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p160/r2.anchor: هو حال من الضمير فى تاركى آلهتنا كأنه قيل وما نترك آلهتنا صادرين عن قولك

NASAFI-FULL:v2p160/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p160/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p160/r3.claim: They say people of their standing cannot believe someone like Hūd, trying to make him despair of their response.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p160/r3.anchor: وما يصح من امثالنا أن يصدقوا مثلك فيما يدعوهم إليه اقناطا له من الإجابة

QURTUBI-FULL:11:50-54/r21.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:50-54/r21.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:11:50-54/r21.claim: They say Hūd brought no clear proof or argument.

QURTUBI-FULL:11:50-54/r22.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:50-54/r22.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:11:50-54/r22.claim: Their refusal to believe him is stubborn persistence in unbelief.

BURSEVI:v4p91#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p91#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p91#2/r3.claim: قالوا begins a new answer, with an implied question asking what Hud's people said after his commands and prohibitions.
BURSEVI:v4p91#2/r3.anchor: قالوا استئناف بتقدير سؤال سائل ، كأنه قيل ما قال : له قومه بعد أن أمرهم ونهاهم فقيل.

BURSEVI:v4p91#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p91#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p91#2/r4.claim: They deny receiving proof despite the miracles, out of extreme obstinacy, like Quraysh asking for a sign after many signs had come.
BURSEVI:v4p91#2/r4.anchor: كما قالت : قريش لرسول الله لولا أنزل عليه آية من ربه مع فوات آياته الحصر

BURSEVI:v4p91#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p91#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p91#2/r5.claim: They mean they will not abandon worship of their idols.
BURSEVI:v4p91#2/r5.anchor: وما نحن بتاركي آلهتنا أي : بتاركي عبادتهم وأصله تاركين سقطت النون بالإضافة.

BURSEVI:v4p91#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p91#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p91#2/r6.claim: The nūn of تاركين is dropped because the active participle is annexed to آلهتنا.

BURSEVI:v4p91#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p91#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p91#2/r7.claim: عن قولك is a circumstantial phrase tied to the pronoun in تاركي: they will not leave their idols because of Hud's words.
BURSEVI:v4p91#2/r7.anchor: عن قولك حال من الضمير في تاركي ، كأنه قيل : وما نترك آلهتنا صادرين عن قولك

BURSEVI:v4p91#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p91#2/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p91#2/r8.claim: The circumstantial wording makes Hud's words the effective cause of their leaving, a nuance stronger than ب or ل would convey.
BURSEVI:v4p91#2/r8.anchor: ومعناه التعليل على أبلع وجه لدلالته على كونه علة فاعلية ولا يفيده الباء واللام.

BURSEVI:v4p91#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p91#2/r9.speaker: السعدي المفتي
BURSEVI:v4p91#2/r9.claim: Al-Saʿdi al-Mufti suggests that عن can mean بسبب, as in the verse about Abraham's promise.
BURSEVI:v4p91#2/r9.anchor: قال السعدي المفتي : قد يقال : عن للسببية كما في قوله تعالى : إلا عن موعدة وعدها إياه}

BURSEVI:v4p91#2/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p91#2/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p91#2/r10.claim: They will not believe Hud's call to monotheism and abandoning idols, expressly extinguishing his hope that they will respond.
BURSEVI:v4p91#2/r10.anchor: وما نحن لك بمؤمنين} أي : بمصدقين فيما تدعونا إليه من التوحيد وترك عبادة الآلهة وهو إقناط له من الإجابة

RAZI-FULL:v18p11/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p11/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p11/r1.claim: Bayyina means a proof, and is so called because it makes truth distinct from falsehood.
RAZI-FULL:v18p11/r1.anchor: البينة سميت بينة لأنها تبين الحق من الباطل

RAZI-FULL:v18p11/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p11/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p11/r2.claim: Though Hūd had shown miracles, his ignorant opponents denied them and claimed he had shown none.
RAZI-FULL:v18p11/r2.anchor: ومن المعلوم أنه عليه السلام كان قد أظهر المعجزات إلا أن القوم بجهلهم أنكروها

RAZI-FULL:v18p11/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p11/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p11/r3.claim: Al-Rāzī calls their reasoning poor: since they admitted God alone benefits and harms and idols do neither, reason itself should lead them to abandon idol worship, not merely Hūd's word.
RAZI-FULL:v18p11/r3.anchor: كانوا يعترفون بأن النافع والضار هو الله تعالى وأن الأصنام لا تنفع ولا تضر

RAZI-FULL:v18p11/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p11/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p11/r4.claim: Their flat refusal to believe Hūd indicates persistence in blind imitation and denial.
RAZI-FULL:v18p11/r4.anchor: وهذا يدل على الإصرار والتقليد والجحود
